title: The Exponential Maturation In The Days Of Decadence

sense.text:
“After this manner therefore pray ye”: Christ was instructing the disciples how to pray, because often we don’t know what to pray for or how to really pray. So Christ made it simple.

“Our Father which art in heaven”: God is not everybody’s father. The power that created the whole universe is our father, and we are his sons, his daughters, his people, his children. That is what makes us near to him. Everybody else is considered bastards. That might sound rough, but this truth is about telling the truth, not about antagonizing anybody: we have to speak the facts.

“Thy kingdom come”: Christ told us to pray to the Lord for his kingdom to be set up on earth. We are joint heirs with him, so when we pray for his kingdom we are praying for our kingdom as well.

“Thy will be done in earth, as it is in heaven.” If the will of God is going to be done in this earth, and there is a will here already, then the will that is here has to be destroyed. Two kings cannot sit on the same throne. There is a will at work right now that is not the will of God, except in this sense: it is the will of God concerning the wicked, because he is the Almighty and he gave them a time period.

So every time you say this prayer, you are praying for the destruction of your enemies, the destruction of this present kingdom. Christ’s kingdom is not going to rule beside Babylon the Great; Christ ain’t setting no throne beside the president. He is going to destroy all of this mess and set up his kingdom. And while that is coming, we have to exponentially mature, grow and organize into the nation the Most High meant for us to be, in the days of this kingdom’s decadence.

precepts.why:
When the apostles were come together they asked Christ, “Lord, wilt thou at this time restore again the kingdom to Israel?” The kingdom is restored to Israel. So Christ’s kingdom is Israel’s kingdom as well.

That is why we ask for Christ to bring the kingdom: we are joint heirs with him. When we pray “Thy kingdom come”, we are asking for the kingdom of Israel.

David said, “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The laws of God are within our hearts. We want what God wants, and that is the will we are praying to be done in earth.

That is why Christ tells us to be perfect, even as our Father is perfect. The objective is for us to become one with him: one with Christ, one with the Most High, one with the angels. That is the hierarchy the Most High is setting up. We are his heirs, his ambassadors on this earth, and that is why he gave us the name Israel: we are the prince of his power. That is us and nobody else.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked.” Notice how the Bible words it: the earth is given. We often bring out that Esau took the planet earth and ruled it in evil, and yes he did, but God gave him the power to do so.

The earth is given into these people’s hands for a time, and when that time is up, it is over. They have the power to do what they are doing now because God orchestrated it.

“He covereth the faces of the judges thereof”: the Most High made the provision for Israel and all the other nations to be covered, so that this man could rule. That is how the whole world came to be deceived about who he is.

“What if God, willing to shew his wrath, and to make his power known”: when God put Esau in power, everybody went ooh and aah over him. He walks around with his chest stuck out, and everybody thinks he is what’s happening. And the Most High says: Wait a minute, I’m the one that put this vagabond up there. This man gets too much glory; let me make it known that I am the one that has all of the power. Babylon the Great shows its wrath when it bombs other countries and steals their resources, their riches, their minds, their women, their gold and bauxite. So the Lord says, what if I want to show my wrath and my power?

“Endured with much longsuffering”: to endure with longsuffering means you want to step in, you want the end of it to come. The Lord is going through longsuffering because he cannot break his word. He gave this man a time period to rule, until the times of the nations be fulfilled. But the Lord has feelings. He is watching this germ, this parasite, getting all the glory, everybody wanting to look like him and have hair like him, setting up a cursed image as his son, calling these rats the Jews while the real Jews are here, trotting up and down our land like it is theirs. The Lord is watching this and he is pissed off.

“The vessels of wrath fitted to destruction”: God made the whole race and nation of Edom the vessels of his wrath. A vessel is something you channel things through, the way a straw channels a drink. The Lord is going to channel how angry and how powerful he is by destroying Esau. Esau was made to be destroyed; that is his whole purpose in being created. God let him be the terrible one everybody is afraid of, the one making it hard for everybody else, just as he set up King Pharaoh, so that the terribleness of God’s power would be seen when he destroys him and he exists no more.

These are diabolical, demonic people; look at how they dragged James Byrd through the streets of Jasper, Texas. That is not teaching hatred; it is the facts. You are walking into a room full of poisonous rattlesnakes trying to figure out which one is nice. There is no such thing as a nice snake. Stick by the commandments: come out from among them, be separate, gather yourselves together, organize and prepare for the kingdom that is coming while he brings this kingdom down. That is the message of this class.

sense.text:
“What shall be the parting asunder of the times?” That is what the prophet Ezra asked, and what the apostles and disciples asked, and what we are all still asking: when is our kingdom coming? What sign should I look for to let me and my people know that our kingdom is come? Asunder means the separation of the times: the time of Esau’s world and our world.

“Or when shall be the end of the first”: the end of the first world that we are subjugated to and in bondage under, the end of this captivity, this hardship, mistreatment and all the evils we face. “And the beginning of it that followeth”: the beginning of our kingdom, where the saints can rejoice in glory. That is what we pray for when we pray for his will to be done in earth. Christ told the disciples to watch the signs of the times; he gave Ezra the answer even more descriptively.

“From Abraham unto Isaac, when Jacob and Esau were born of him”: anybody going to church or reading the Bible who wants to find out when the kingdom of God is coming has to go back to Genesis and pay attention to these two boys. The churches don’t talk about this. The black preacher in the church doesn’t know a damn thing, but the elite people over them know where the key parts are, and they gave the preachers a curriculum of love garbage so the people never learn this. That is why they have so many problems with the Israelites: we are literally teaching what the Bible says, and persecution comes because of it.

Jacob’s hand held on to the heel of Esau for a reason, and the next verse gives it: “For” means because.

“For Esau is the end of the world”: because Esau is the end of the world. When the disciples, the apostles and the prophets asked about the end of the world and the sign, the answer is: pay attention to Esau. The preachers try to make him ambiguous, as if nobody knows who he is or as if the Edomites were destroyed, to keep you from knowing when it is coming. The sign is here and we are in it now. Esau is the symbol of the destruction that is going down; God put him up there for that reason, and there is nothing special about him at all.

“And Jacob is the beginning of it that followeth”: Jacob is the beginning of the kingdom that follows. When Esau goes down, we are coming up. When Esau is destroyed, we are in our kingdom. That is the whole key.

Back in the ’80s, working in an electronics store in Manhattan, the Bishop guessed that the Chinese or the Japanese would rule the world next. A sister answered, no, the black man is going to rule next. She did not know who Jacob and Esau were, but her statement was right, and there it is in the Bible.

“The hand of man is betwixt the heel and the hand”: the hand of man is the nations. Between the rulership of Esau and the rulership of Jacob, the nations are in the middle. They are never going to run this whole planet; they will always be subject to one or the other. Not the Japanese, not the Chinese. The only one to completely dominate was Esau, and the Lord gave him that power for his glory, to destroy him. Then he is going to give us the power to rule this planet in righteousness forever.

precepts.why:
The disciples came to Christ privately on the mount of Olives, “saying, Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world?” It is the same thing the apostles asked, the same thing Ezra asked, the same thing we all ask every time we pray for his kingdom to come.

You are literally praying for the destruction of this kingdom. We are not trying to stay here. We are trying to exponentially mature into the nation the Lord needs us to be, the organized nation in the midst of this kingdom, so that we can properly inherit the kingdom.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven”: that is the sign we are looking for, the Son of man “coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.” Then “he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” This is what Israel wants, and the Lord is telling us how to prepare for it: by gathering together and organizing into that one real body.

“Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh.” When the buds start to unfurl, you know spring is here and summer is coming, so you prepare, the way you winterize your car before winter. The tender branches come in the springtime, which is how you know the year really begins in the spring; nothing grows in the dead of winter. When you start to see things happening in this system, you know that Christ is on the way.

“So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.” When you see the decadence of this society, know that the tribulation and the destruction is near, even at the doors. That is what is happening all over this planet now. So when Ezra asked about the parting asunder of the times, Christ answered it here: watch the signs of the times.

sense.text:
We are learning that the destruction of our enemies is at hand and the decadence is out here. The president of the superpower, the king of the planet, with bombs to bomb anybody at any moment, has to hide in a catering cart flying to Turkey. That is how the Most High is bringing decadence to this whole system. When officials of the superpower have to put out a Save America Act, they are saying something without saying it: the real meaning is that Babylon the Great has to be saved, because the Israelites are coming with this Bible. They are not worried about regular blacks or black pastors; they are worried about the twelve tribes finding out who they are and waking up our people. The Deacon added that they are turning the federal government into an army on this soil and building detention centers, and they are not for immigrants: they are for the sons of God. And your vote means nothing: when Bush invaded Panama in 1989, the United Nations condemned it as a flagrant violation of international law, and they went anyway.

“In the days of these kings”: the kings are all the kingdoms that ruled this planet, the great image Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of and Daniel interpreted in this chapter: Babylon the head of gold, then Persia, then Greece, then Rome, and America last. We are in the last part of this beast right now. “Shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed”: all the other kingdoms will be destroyed.

In the days of these kings, during their rulership, while the decadence is setting in, the Most High is causing us to get ourselves together, and persecution is going to be part of that. We are to build while we are still here, not to add on to this kingdom, but to prepare for the kingdom that is coming.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people”: not to other races or other nations; it is only for the twelve tribes of Israel. “But it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms”: Christ is going to destroy them all. That is what the disciples and the apostles were asking about.

precepts.why:
“I beheld till the thrones were cast down”: Daniel saw in the vision the same kingdoms of chapter 2 brought down, the four great kings destroyed, and then the Most High sat down and judged them.

“And the Ancient of days did sit”: the Ancient of days is the Most High, here before days began. He sat, so he had a body, with legs. “Whose garment was white as snow”: he had a garment on his body, not like a ghost flying in the wind. “And the hair of his head like the pure wool”: if he had hair on his head, he had a body. He had a form like a man, so that we could describe him. He was not a lizard or some other creature; as Exodus says, the Lord is a man of war.

Like the pure wool is like the pure negro hair, woolly black man’s hair. That is our King, that is our Creator, and his Son looks just like him. That is what is coming to us when the thrones are cast down.

sense.text:
The decadence begins in the mind first. They don’t want this Bible properly taught because it affects how you think and how you act, and the whole world is going to be forced to bow down to what is in it. They want to rule over the children of Israel forever. We are the people everybody has to keep watch on, because God is watching this people.

“Thus saith the Lord God concerning Edom”: this is about Edom, and the question is, who is Edom? “We have heard a rumour from the Lord”: part of the rumour is who Esau is, and once the world finds out who Esau really is, it is over. That part of the rumour is us bringing it out, pointing the finger at Edom so the nations hear what he is doing. “And an ambassador is sent among the heathen”: that is the other part of the rumour.

The truth being brought out about him is what bothers Esau, and what bothers his minions, the black preachers that serve Esau and serve Christianity.

precepts.why:
“They that see thee shall narrowly look upon thee, and consider thee, saying, Is this the man”: that is total astonishment. You mean to tell me we have been on this earth all this time and you are the Edomite this Bible is talking about? You are the devil? People will be blown away because the secrets are revealed. What they told me in church, in school, on TV, all lies.

“Is this the man that made the earth to tremble”: why are the nations going to figure him out? A young brother in the class answered it exactly: because the prophets are going to bring out the truth. People are hearing it and realizing the white man is the devil. And they know it themselves: now they say embrace it, embrace your whiteness, you don’t have to apologize, yes, we’re Satan.

So their mission is to stop us from teaching. If they can stop this teaching from going out, they can rule a little longer. The more we bring out the prophecies and show the world who this man is, the worse it gets for them. That is where the persecution comes from, and why they send black preachers after the Israelites to make sure our people don’t wake up.

“Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his!” This is how the nations will point their finger at Edom, the same thing Isaiah said.

Everywhere he has gone, he stole. Everybody is going to say: That doesn’t belong to you. You’re the evil, you’re the wicked, get out of my land. That is the rumour coming out.

Our job in bringing this rumour out is to prophesy about destruction, to bring out what they don’t want taught: that they are Edom, that they are Esau, the wicked the Bible talks about. The Bible says that wicked shall be revealed, and he is revealed because we reveal him. As long as people think he is Jesus Christ, the Jews and the Christians, he continues in his evil. The Lord says it is time for him to come down and for his prophets to be lifted up, so persecution and hatred will be ramped up, and we had better come together for real.

Jeremiah stood before the Israelites: “The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.” Not only Jeremiah but the prophets before him prophesied the same thing, and we are doing the same thing now. Every time it comes around we get closer to our kingdom.

The things we see today were not seen when this was written, not in the time of Rome, of Jeremiah or of Isaiah. Esau and Jacob, that whole dynamic, is in our face now. When the apostles asked if the kingdom would be restored then, the answer was no: there had to come a falling away first, and we had to go completely down. Now we are in the time. And pestilence and sicknesses come because our people are still playing with sin, lying and deceit; they have to hear that the Most High is about to bring judgment.

That is why the black preachers are mad, and why some of your own family don’t want to hear the Bible: it brings division, as Christ said he came to bring. The trees are unfurling; the season is here.

sense.text:
It is time for us to mature while this decadence is happening right at our feet, and to understand what we need to be doing despite what is happening.

“Flee out of the midst of Babylon”: the same thing said in Revelation and in 2 Corinthians. It is not necessarily getting on a plane, because this whole earth is corrupted. It means come out of the philosophies of Babylon the Great, out of how this system has us thinking.

“And deliver every man his soul”: repent, and don’t go back to those lies. “Be not cut off in her iniquity”: don’t be partakers of her sins, as Revelation says; don’t be destroyed when the evil comes through. “For this is the time of the Lord’s vengeance”: we are in that time now. The Most High is slapping the heads of these leaders, making them look stupid and crazy, in our presence. You think your vote is going to change that?

“He will render unto her a recompence”: a payback to our enemies. The Lord says return to me and I will destroy your enemies. We return by obeying his commandments and organizing as the scriptures say, becoming that mature nation in exponential growth, so that when we get the kingdom we know how to act and operate as a nation. We are in the training ground. We were brought into captivity only to learn a lesson, because we did not want to serve our Lord; when we learn it well, we come off our punishment and enjoy the kingdom.

“Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand”: written around the time of ancient Babylon, but it is prophecy of Babylon the Great. America became a golden cup by robbing everybody else’s gold and diamonds, then held it up in the New York Harbor and told the nations: if you want success, you have to come here, or you will live with mud floors in your huts. That is the American dream, after she stole it all from them.

“The nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad”: the nations are crazy and mad because their economies, their livelihood and their way of life are destroyed, and democracy and Christianity have obliterated the minds of people all around the world.

“Babylon is suddenly fallen and destroyed”: past tense. Jeremiah stood with the brothers before Babylon the Great even existed, and already gave the past tense of that future Babylon, already destroyed.

“Take balm for her pain, if so be she may be healed”: they are trying to heal Babylon today with these preachers. You can’t stop it; it is going down.

“We would have healed Babylon, but she is not healed”: the Lord says it is not healing; it is time for it to be destroyed. So where should our minds be? On that righteous exponential maturation, getting ready for the coming kingdom.

“Forsake her, and let us go every one into his own country”: let her go; come to your own country, your own nation. “For her judgment reacheth unto heaven, and is lifted up even to the skies”: the same thing Revelation says of her sins reaching unto heaven, and what Obadiah says of Edom exalting himself, the space garbage she put out there, when the Lord says he will bring him down. There was no space travel when Jeremiah brought this out; now we understand what it is talking about.

“The Lord hath brought forth our righteousness: come, and let us declare in Zion the work of the Lord our God.” We understand the message: return to him, build among ourselves, learn to be that proper nation, while the Lord mocks Babylon the Great.

“Make bright the arrows; gather the shields: the Lord hath raised up the spirit of the kings of the Medes: for his device is against Babylon, to destroy it.” They are getting their weapons ready; the Most High has them. The device is the bomb, the nuclear bomb. They built the silos and the missiles and say they will never press the button; they are going to press every button there is. God caused the smith, the scientist, to build the weapon of their own destruction. “Because it is the vengeance of the Lord, the vengeance of his temple.”

“Set up the standard upon the walls of Babylon”: the standard is the Bible, the troublemaker. Walls represent stability; we trusted in the walls around Jerusalem, and the walls of Jericho came tumbling down. The Lord sets his Bible upon the walls of Babylon to break their stability.

“Make the watch strong, set up the watchmen, prepare the ambushes”: the ambushes are the terrorists. The Most High already has them sent here; they grew up in your backyard and blend right in. “For the Lord hath both devised and done that which he spake against the inhabitants of Babylon”: Jeremiah is already seeing the aftermath of the destruction.

“O thou that dwellest upon many waters”: Babylon the Great dwells upon many waters with her battleships and her military all over the planet. “Abundant in treasures”: abundant in everybody else’s treasures, because with that power she stole everybody’s riches. That is why Habakkuk says woe to him that increaseth that which is not his.

“Thine end is come”: the end of them, already spoken as done. That is what the disciples and the prophets were asking: when is the end coming? When this man goes down, that is it; that is the Esau and Jacob of 2 Esdras 6.

“And the measure of thy covetousness”: the measure of her evils has come up to God’s nostrils. God says, I’m sick of you. He endured with much longsuffering the vessels of wrath, made to be destroyed, while they paraded themselves as the people of God.

“The Lord of hosts hath sworn by himself”: he didn’t ask anybody else for permission; he swore on his own name. There is no getting out of this; no preacher and nobody else can stop it.

“Surely I will fill thee with men, as with caterpillers”: terrorists. The Most High is going to fill this place with men from the other nations who are mad at what Babylon the Great did to their places. She took their riches, their diamonds and their gold, then told them to come over to work; they are working to get inside the system to take it down. These are the sleeper cells. So we don’t need to be playing games while this is happening. Whether we are ready or not, the Most High is going to bring it to pass.

precepts.why:
“And I heard another voice from heaven, saying, Come out of her, my people”: get your head out of Christianity, out of the philosophies, out of thinking your vote will mean something. Israelites, get your mind right about what the Most High is about to bring on this earth.

“That ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues”: Zephaniah and Jeremiah say the same thing in different words. Be not cut off in her iniquity; come out so that you don’t get caught up in the judgments.

“Gather yourselves together, yea, gather together, O nation not desired”: he is not asking. That is a commandment, a direct order. None of the nations desire us, so we are obligated to come together in righteousness and follow the program in this Bible.

“Before the decree bring forth”: before the destruction comes. “Before the fierce anger of the Lord come upon you.” We have to gather together so that we don’t get caught in those things. It is the same as Revelation: that ye be not partakers of her sins and receive not of her plagues. You can’t learn to be a nation sitting at home online; we have to come together, and that is a commandment.

“Wherefore come out from among them, and be ye separate, saith the Lord”: the same thing again. Separate your thinking from their thinking. You are not supposed to be hanging around them and hanging out with them; that is wrong, no matter what they tell you. It sounds like racist talk, but we are the victims of every level of racism, and when we say stay away from them, all of a sudden we are the racists. The hell with that. Our sons end up dead messing around with them.

“And touch not the unclean thing”: if you keep messing around in their philosophies, their religions and their politics, it will pollute you and you will be destroyed by it.

“And I will receive you, and will be a Father unto you, and ye shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty.” We will be received in the Most High’s nation. He builds that kingdom when you come away from them. Some will lose mothers, fathers, sons and daughters for this truth, but when you come into it you will gain them back sevenfold, tenfold. As Zephaniah said, he is gathering you up.

This is how Babylon made the nations drunk. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers. He who smote the people in wrath with a continual stroke”: that is Babylon the Great, who smote the nations in her anger. This is the same Lucifer of the same chapter, the man the nations shall narrowly look upon.

In wrath, the wrath of her fornication: she got the nations in bed with her, and when you fornicate with a harlot you become one. Now they are mad and crazy because they are in love with a whore they can’t stand.

“With a continual stroke”: a continual killing. America continually drops bombs on people, puts embargoes on them, rips them off, never lets them get up. “He that ruled the nations in anger”: that is how they talk on television. “Is persecuted”: now it is their time to come down. That is why Habakkuk says all the nations will take up a parable against him; they all see it and are turning against her now.

Isaiah does the same thing Jeremiah did. “Come near, ye nations, to hear; and hearken, ye people: let the earth hear”: the Lord wants everybody to hear what he is about to do on this planet. “For the indignation of the Lord is upon all nations, and his fury upon all their armies: he hath utterly destroyed them, he hath delivered them to the slaughter.” It does not say he will; it says he hath. Isaiah saw the same past tense of the destruction that Jeremiah saw.

“Their slain also shall be cast out, and their stink shall come up out of their carcases, and the mountains shall be melted with their blood”: dead bodies all over the streets, the smell of the flesh, their governments melted with their blood. This goes into Revelation 18.

“And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved”: the host of their kingdom. “And the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll”: rolled together as a mushroom cloud, a nuclear bomb. “And all their host shall fall down”: their armies and military, done as easily as “the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.”

“For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea”: God’s sword bathed in Esau’s heaven, and the Lord tells you who he is talking about: Edom. He is the devil the Bible speaks of, the one the Lord has his war with, the one on the scene at the end, where Esau is the end of the world and Jacob the beginning of it that followeth. When he goes down, we are up next. The Deacon added that people say this was a war in heaven with Lucifer in the past, but it is the future: the prophets already saw Christ fighting America and Europe and destroying them, and recorded it so we would know.

The Most High is sick of them. “The Lord shall go forth as a mighty man, he shall stir up jealousy like a man of war: he shall cry, yea, roar; he shall prevail against his enemies.” The Lord gave Esau his time to rule, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled. Until then he has to watch this germ move around like he is something great. When their time is up, when he gets loose from his prophecies, he is free to deal with them.

“I have long time holden my peace”: that is the longsuffering of Romans 9. “I have been still, and refrained myself”: he had to hold himself back. He wants to step in while they parade themselves as his people and take advantage of his real children, and he is mad as hell, but he is a man of his word and lets the prophecies finish out.

“Now will I cry like a travailing woman; I will destroy and devour at once.” Now means he is free: the prophecies have been met, that number of the Israelites has woken up, and he is no longer held back.

“And the great dragon was cast out”: the same Edomite we have been reading about, the great red dragon, Edom, Idumea. Cast out of his heaven, his rulership. “That old serpent, called the Devil, and Satan”: he gets his power from the spiritual demon Satan.

“Which deceiveth the whole world”: there is no Bible on the planet that says Jesus looks like Charles Manson, yet all the nations, black people included, hold up that white image and call it Jesus. As a matter of fact, Jesus is described as a black man. Only a king-sized deceiver could do that: he made everybody think the so-called white people are the Jews and the Christians, and that we, the jewels of God, are nothing. He covered the faces of the judges thereof.

“Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ”: that is the same now as Isaiah 42, when the Lord is free to get loose, because the dragon above was cast out. The times of the nations are fulfilled and we are ready to rule. “For the accuser of our brethren is cast down”: the one that lied about us and lied on us is destroyed.

sense.text:
This Bible will influence not only our enemies’ demise but also us, to get ourselves right and organize and be in the acceptance of the Most High. It was important for Babylon the Great to make us feel unworthy of the Lord’s goodness: hanging us on trees, drowning us, riddling our bodies with bullets, our children turning up drowned with organs missing, like Rasheem Carter, and still we are not upset enough to organize. The Deacon said our people won’t gather together until things get bad, until they lose their jobs, because they still trust in their oppressor and love the white man in their minds. The Most High will force us.

“Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered”: that is us, the twelve tribes, scattered all over the planet.

“In the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people”: if it was constantly said to us that we are not the Lord’s people, we internalize it and live like it. That is how a negative influence changes your reality. Tell your children they are nothing and they will be nothing; tell them they are great and they will be great. When television, media, books and history lie to us everywhere we turn, we never believe anything great could come from us.

“There it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God”: in the very places of our captivity where we were taught we are not God’s people, the Most High opens up the Bible to change how we see ourselves. While the decadence pours down on this system, we are being awakened, because the prophets are out here teaching it. Our enemies are angry because we are undoing what they did to us, mainly through Christianity, where we sat clapping with a Bible learning nothing about ourselves, our condition or our deliverance, so ashamed we can’t even talk about recompense.

“For wisdom, which is the worker of all things, taught me”: this is the same wisdom of verse 25, the breath of the power of God. It is what will change the negative way we see ourselves, the thinking that we cannot organize, cannot come together, cannot build and prepare for when Christ comes and we set the whole planet in its proper order. We are not learning that under Christianity.

“Undefiled, plain, not subject to hurt, loving the thing that is good”: the wisdom of God is undefiled. Wisdom will properly guide us in everything we seek to move on and every endeavour we seek to make happen. Not just any kind of wisdom: God’s wisdom.

“For wisdom is more moving than any motion”: a lot of people think strength comes from everything but wisdom. When you have a mind of wisdom, you can do anything. If God’s wisdom operates in our thinking, the whole planet can change, because everything on this planet is a result of thought.

If our enemies caused us to look at ourselves as nothing, we became that, and everything behind it is destroyed. This breath has to come in and undo that damage, and then the greatness waiting inside us comes out.

“For she is the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty: therefore can no defiled thing fall into her.” This wisdom is the change that is going to come into the brothers and sisters and wake them up. Notice the word breath: the same word as in Ezekiel 37. That pure influence cannot be stopped; once we have it, we have it.

precepts.why:
God’s wisdom, not just any wisdom. “Howbeit we speak wisdom among them that are perfect: yet not the wisdom of this world”: we don’t speak the wisdom of the people out here who think they have real wisdom. We speak God’s wisdom, God’s commandments.

“Nor of the princes of this world, that come to nought”: their wisdom is not God’s wisdom, and the Lord is going to bring it all down. It is our wisdom that will take that authority in this society.

This breath is how we are made ready to become those exponentially mature brothers and sisters of this nation. “The bones came together, bone to his bone. And when I beheld, lo, the sinews and the flesh came up upon them, and the skin covered them above: but there was no breath in them.” In the ’60s we had the desire and the fortitude and made great strides, but the wisdom of the Bible was not there to bring forth the real maturation of the nation. Now we are getting the wisdom that is going to bring this whole system down and lift us up.

“Come from the four winds, O breath, and breathe upon these slain, that they may live. So I prophesied as he commanded me, and the breath came into them”: this wisdom came into our brothers.

“And they lived, and stood up upon their feet, an exceeding great army”: an army of organized brothers who know how to deal with their families and with the nation, how to keep God’s commandments, how to keep order in our sanctuaries, how to set up teams and set the nation up. This wisdom teaches the commandments and how to be proper brothers, proper sisters and proper children. That is what was missing in the ’60s.

sense.text:
Our job in teaching this wisdom is to teach our brothers and sisters to keep the commandments and the faith of Christ. “Here are they that keep the commandments of God”: this wisdom teaches us to keep the commandments of God. “And the faith of Jesus”: you have to have both.

Without faith you cannot please God. If you don’t have faith, you will give up; if you have faith in what you are aspiring to, there is no stopping you. Your faith turns on the works. You can’t say you have faith and not work toward it, because faith without works is dead. With unyielding faith, everything you do will be according to that faith, and you will do it because you believe in it. All of this is how we mature exponentially.

precepts.why:
“Good Master, what shall I do that I may inherit eternal life?” What shall I do to get the kingdom? There are people, pastors and churches, who say they love Jesus and love this Bible. This man knew the Bible: Christ told him, “Thou knowest the commandments.” He was raised up to keep them.

“Do not commit adultery, Do not kill, Do not steal, Do not bear false witness, Defraud not, Honour thy father and mother.” While we are in this captivity we are not supposed to be stealing, committing adultery, murdering or bearing false witness. Defraud not: don’t lie to each other. We are supposed to learn how to operate as a righteous people in this captivity.

Matthew recorded the same incident. “If thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments.” “Thou shalt do no murder”: that is what thou shalt not kill means in Exodus 20.

“Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself”: want for your neighbour the same thing you want for yourself. You would not want anybody to deceive you or do you dirty, so why would you do that to somebody else? If we just learned that, we would be all right.

“All these things have I kept from my youth up: what lack I yet?” Christ told him, “go and sell that thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven: and come and follow me.” “He went away sorrowful: for he had great possessions.” He could not do it because he did not have faith in what Christ was saying. He could keep all the rest, but without faith that he would actually get the kingdom, he could not go that far. Without faith you will not endure. The commandments and the faith go together; you can’t have one without the other, and your faith is what drives you to keep the commandments.

In Birth of a Nation, Nate Parker played Nat Turner being whipped with a smile on his face. Like the apostles who rejoiced when they were beaten, he knew he was persecuted for righteousness’ sake. To endure what we have to go through, we need faith beyond the trial and beyond the moment. His spirit was already beyond it. Suffer not as a murderer, but as a Christian.

“Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you”: “But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings.” He endured it for a worthy cause; they cut his body up, but he preached the word of the Lord. “That, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy”: that is us in the kingdom. All we went through will be like a bad dream. That is what our faith is for.

“On their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified”: they speak evil about Christ and about us dealing with the Most High in this program, but God is glorified because we do what he said.

“But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men’s matters”: breaking the laws of the Most High is not a reason to suffer. That is why we must keep the commandments of God. “Yet if any man suffer as a Christian”: as one who keeps the commandments of God and follows Christ, not this Christianity. “Let him not be ashamed; but let him glorify God on this behalf.”

“For the time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God”: that is why we have to get ourselves together first and be the example. “And if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?” Our brothers and sisters who want no part of this Bible, the Most High is going to destroy completely.

How strong is faith? In the Ten Commandments film, Rameses is asked if he believes the slave deliverer is a myth, and answers that what he believes is of no account: what matters is that the slaves believe in him. If they believe they will be delivered, you can’t do anything with them. A man who straps explosives to himself believing he will get seventy virgins, there is nothing you can do with a man like that, because that is his faith. When we have faith in this Bible like that, we are unshakable and unstoppable, even if they kill us, and some of us are going to be killed. After you hang me, kiss my ass: that is the attitude you have to have. With a knife to their neck, some will say they will eat the pork, and they might preserve their life a few days longer, but nobody respects a traitor.

sense.text:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”: we love this scripture, because when they say it, they are telling you they know who Esau is. You are blasting an Edomite in a camp because he is the devil the Bible speaks of, and he comes back with thou shalt not abhor an Edomite. He is confirming that he is Esau. We don’t hate you; God does. But that is not the point.

“Thou shalt not abhor an Egyptian”: nobody talks about the Egyptian; most don’t even know that part is in the verse. The Lord is a mastermind: he put Esau and Egypt in the same verse because both are pivotal in what we are reading. Both had us in horrible captivity.

precepts.why:
This scripture was in the lesson because of what Jeremiah told us in captivity. “Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them”: even though we were going to be in Babylon only seventy years, we were told to do this. So we should follow that example.

“Take ye wives, and beget sons and daughters; and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands”, “that ye may be increased there, and not diminished.” We have to do these things in the days of our captivity, in the days of these kings, as Daniel 2:44 reads, with the right mind and the wisdom that influences our righteous behaviour among each other.

“And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives”: seeking the peace of the city does not mean watering down the Bible, half preaching it or diluting it, the way the black pastors lie on the word of God to appease Esau. We cannot do that. We have to teach the Bible the way it is, and if it upsets you, too bad.

Why Esau and Egypt together? Romans 9 shows it. Who is the chapter talking about? “Jacob have I loved, but Esau have I hated.” The subject matter is Esau.

“For the scripture saith unto Pharaoh, Even for this same purpose have I raised thee up”: for means because. The statement is pushed to Esau: the reason you were raised up, the reason you have the power you have now, is that the Lord did the same thing to Pharaoh. Even for this same purpose: your time now, Esau. He raised you up, gave you weapons and all this power, made you rule over the earth, so that when he destroys you everybody will know that he is God and there is no other.

“That I might shew my power in thee, and that my name might be declared throughout all the earth”: when the Lord destroys Esau as the vessels of his wrath, as he destroyed ancient Pharaoh, his name will be declared all over the earth.

“Therefore hath he mercy on whom he will have mercy, and whom he will he hardeneth.” He chose to harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he has chosen to harden Trump’s heart and Babylon the Great’s heart, so they go proudly kicking over people’s land and taking it. God has them thinking that way. You can’t stop him from being the anointed cherub; you can’t stop him from being the devil. The Lord made him that way.

“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: that is the valley of dry bones in Ezekiel, where the wisdom comes to wake you up. The great city is America, the greatest city on the planet, where everybody is trying to get to; the same Babylon Isaiah and Jeremiah spoke of.

“Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”: not the actual Egypt or Sodom, but spiritually it has both traits, the traits of sodomy and the traits of Egypt. We are the result of that slavery. That is why the Lord put the Edomite and the Egyptian in the same verse. “Where also our Lord was crucified”: Christianity; they lied to us, and the destroying doctrine mainly comes out of here.

“And shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”: because they are not physically dead. The dry bones in the valley were a figure of our condition today; we are like dead men, and the breath has to come upon us to wake us up.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet”: that spirit is the wisdom of Wisdom of Solomon 7:25. “Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud; and their enemies beheld them.” That is when Esau’s kingdom is destroyed, 2 Esdras 6:7-9 right there: our enemies will see us delivered while they are being destroyed.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake”: the destruction, the bombs. “And the tenth part of the city fell”: the city with the ten horns, America. “And in the earthquake were slain of men seven thousand”: seven means completion, thousands and thousands of dead bodies, as Isaiah 34 says their stink shall come up out of their carcases. All these scriptures go together. “And the remnant were affrighted, and gave glory to the God of heaven”: we will be afraid when we see all that destruction come down, but we will give glory to the Most High for delivering us.
